question: A combination vehicle falls into Class A when it has a gross combination weight rating (GCWR) of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of the towed vehicle(s) exceeds what amount?
explanation: Class A Combination Vehicles are any combination with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the towed vehicle(s) is more than 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classifications

question: A single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not exceeding 10,000 pounds GVWR, falls into which CDL class?
explanation: Class B 'Heavy Straight Vehicles' covers any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, including straight trucks and large buses.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classifications

question: A single vehicle under 26,001 pounds GVWR (Class C) only requires a CDL if it meets which additional condition?
choice_a: It is designed to carry 16 or more passengers (including the driver), or it must be placarded for hazardous materials
choice_b: It travels more than 150 miles from its base
choice_c: It has more than two axles
choice_d: It is painted a commercial color
explanation: Class C vehicles under 26,001 lbs GVWR are included in the CDL program only if designed to carry 16+ passengers or used to transport hazardous materials requiring placarding.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classifications

question: A driver who holds a valid Class A CDL may also legally operate vehicles classified under which other groups, absent restrictions?
choice_a: Neither Class B nor Class C without a separate test
choice_b: Both Class B and Class C
explanation: Since Class A skills include those required for Classes B and C, a driver with a Class A license may also drive vehicles in Classes B and C.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classifications

question: Which of the following vehicles requires a CDL regardless of its GVWR?
choice_a: Any size vehicle carrying material requiring hazardous materials placards
choice_b: A golf cart used on a private course
choice_c: A pickup truck used to run personal errands
choice_d: A rental car used for a business trip
explanation: Any size vehicle requiring hazmat placards, or carrying a select agent or toxin under 42 CFR Part 73, requires a CDL regardless of weight.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classifications

question: Which CDL endorsement is required for any driver, regardless of vehicle class, who wants to haul a quantity of material designated hazardous under 49 U.S.C. 5103 that must be placarded?
explanation: The Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement is required for any driver, regardless of vehicle class, hauling material required to be placarded under subpart F of 49 CFR Part 172.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: The X endorsement is issued to drivers of tank vehicles who also haul placarded hazardous materials. It shows the driver has passed which knowledge exams?
choice_b: Both the tank vehicle and hazardous materials exams
choice_d: The passenger and school bus exams
explanation: The Combination Hazardous Materials and Tank Vehicle (X) endorsement shows the driver has passed the special knowledge examinations for both tank vehicles and hazardous materials.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: The Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement applies to a tank with an individual rated capacity of more than how many gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of at least how many gallons?
explanation: The Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement applies to tanks with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: The Double/Triple Trailers (T) endorsement may only be added to which class of CDL?
choice_c: Any class, A, B, or C
explanation: The T endorsement is for drivers qualified for Class A vehicles who wish to pull double or triple trailers.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: Which endorsement applies to a vehicle designed to carry 16 or more people (including the driver), and may apply to a bus in any class (A, B, or C)?
explanation: The Passenger (P) endorsement applies to drivers of vehicles with a design capacity of 16 or more people, including the driver, in any CDL class.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: According to the manual, which endorsements are the ONLY ones that may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
choice_a: Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank Vehicle (N)
choice_c: None; no endorsement may ever be added to a CLP
explanation: The manual states the only endorsements that may be added to a CLP are Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank Vehicle (N).
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: Under Missouri rules, to obtain a Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement an applicant must be at least what age and meet what citizenship/residency status?
choice_c: 21 years old, a U.S. citizen or permanent resident alien
choice_d: There is no minimum age, only a background check
explanation: Missouri requires H endorsement applicants to be at least 21 years of age and a U.S. citizen or permanent resident alien, and to pass the hazmat written test and a security threat assessment.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14 - Missouri Commercial Driver License Information

question: In Missouri, a School Bus (S) endorsement applicant must be at least what age, and drivers aged 75 or over must do what?
choice_a: 25 years old; retake the written knowledge test annually
choice_b: 21 years old; automatically surrender the endorsement
choice_d: 21 years old; complete mandatory skills retesting of basic and on-road driving skills at least biennially
explanation: School bus endorsement applicants must be 21 or older, and endorsement holders aged 75 or over must complete mandatory skills retesting at least biennially, with a license term not to exceed two years.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14 - Missouri Commercial Driver License Information, Endorsements

question: Restriction code 'E' is applied to a CDL when the skills test is performed in what type of vehicle?
choice_b: A vehicle equipped with an automatic transmission
choice_c: A vehicle with a fifth-wheel connection
choice_d: A vehicle equipped with air brakes
explanation: If an applicant performs the skills test in a vehicle equipped with an automatic transmission, the state must restrict the CDL from operating a manual transmission CMV (restriction E).
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Restrictions

question: Restriction code 'K' restricts a driver to what type of operation?
choice_b: Intrastate driving only, no interstate commerce
explanation: The K restriction is applied when an applicant certifies Non-Excepted or Excepted Intrastate status, restricting the person from operating a CMV in interstate commerce.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14 - Missouri Commercial Driver License Information, Restrictions

question: How can a driver avoid or remove the 'L' (no air brake) restriction?
choice_a: By taking a defensive driving course
choice_b: It cannot be removed once issued
choice_c: By passing the written air brake test and performing the skills test in a vehicle equipped with air brakes
choice_d: By driving for one year without incident
explanation: The L restriction applies if an applicant does not take or fails the air brake knowledge test, or tests in a vehicle without air brakes; it is avoided by passing the written air brake test and skills test in an air-brake-equipped vehicle.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14 - Missouri Commercial Driver License Information, Restrictions

question: A driver who performs the passenger-endorsement skills test in a Group C vehicle (rather than a Group A vehicle) receives which restriction, prohibiting them from operating a passenger vehicle requiring a Group A or B CDL?
explanation: Restriction N ('No Class A/B Passenger Vehicle') applies when the passenger endorsement skills test is performed in a vehicle requiring a Group C CDL.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Restrictions

question: Restriction 'O' is applied when an applicant's combination-vehicle skills test uses what kind of connection instead of a standard fifth wheel?
choice_c: A pintle hook or other non-fifth-wheel connection
explanation: The O restriction ('No Tractor-Trailer CMV') applies when the combination vehicle skills test used a pintle hook or other non-fifth-wheel connection for a Group A CDL.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14 - Missouri Commercial Driver License Information, Restrictions

question: A CLP issued with a Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement must also carry which restriction?
choice_b: X - No cargo in a CMV tank vehicle
choice_c: P - No passengers in a CMV bus
explanation: If a CLP is issued with a Tanker (N) endorsement, it must also contain an X restriction (No cargo in a CMV tank vehicle).
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: Restriction code 'V' indicates what on a driver's CDLIS record?
choice_a: That the driver's vehicle has air brakes
choice_b: That the driver failed the vision test
choice_c: That the driver is a military veteran
choice_d: That the driver has a medical variance on file
explanation: Restriction V indicates the driver has been issued a medical variance, and this is noted on the CDLIS driver record and CDL document.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Restrictions

question: Missouri restriction code 'W' (Farm Waiver) restricts a driver to operating a CMV during what period?
choice_c: Within 25 miles of the farm at all times
choice_d: A specific 180-day period, after which they must operate a noncommercial vehicle for the rest of the year
explanation: The W (Farm Waiver) restriction limits a driver to driving a CMV during a specific 180-day period; the remainder of the year they must operate a noncommercial motor vehicle.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14 - Missouri Commercial Driver License Information, Restrictions

question: Which CDL knowledge test must be taken by ALL commercial driver license applicants, regardless of vehicle class or endorsement sought?
explanation: The general knowledge test is taken by all applicants, regardless of what class or endorsements they seek.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Commercial Driver License Tests

question: The CDL Skills Test consists of three segments that must be taken in a specific order. What is that order?
choice_a: On-road driving, basic vehicle control, vehicle inspection
choice_b: The segments may be taken in any order
choice_c: Basic vehicle control, on-road driving, vehicle inspection
choice_d: Vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, on-road driving
explanation: The CDL Skills Test must be taken in this order: vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, then on-road driving, and each segment must be passed before moving to the next.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Skills Tests

question: A vehicle with components that are marked or labeled (other than by the manufacturer) is subject to what rule for the CDL Skills Test?
choice_b: It must be used only for the vehicle inspection segment
choice_c: It gets an automatic bonus for correct identification
choice_d: It cannot be used for the CDL Skills Test
explanation: Any vehicle that has components marked or labeled (other than by the manufacturer) cannot be used for the CDL Skills Test.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Skills Tests

question: How many questions are on Missouri's General Knowledge CDL written exam?
explanation: The Missouri General Knowledge CDL written exam has 50 questions.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, CDL Written Examinations

question: How many questions are on Missouri's Hazardous Materials endorsement written exam, and how does that compare to the Tank Vehicle endorsement exam?
choice_a: 25 questions; 5 more than the Tank endorsement exam
choice_b: 20 questions; the same as the Tank endorsement exam
choice_c: 50 questions; 30 more than the Tank endorsement exam
choice_d: 30 questions; 10 more than the 20-question Tank endorsement exam
explanation: The Hazardous Materials endorsement exam has 30 questions, while the Tank Vehicle endorsement exam has 20 questions, a difference of 10.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, CDL Written Examinations

question: What minimum score must a Missouri CDL applicant achieve to pass each written exam?
explanation: The manual states applicants must score 80% on each written exam.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, CDL Written Examinations

question: In what language(s) are Missouri's commercial driver license written and skills examinations administered?
choice_a: English, with an interpreter allowed only for the skills test
choice_b: English only, with no interpreter allowed
explanation: Commercial license examinations are administered only in English, and an interpreter is not allowed for any portion of the written or skills examinations.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, CDL Written Examinations

question: Approximately how long does Missouri CDL knowledge testing take, according to the manual?
choice_c: 1-2 hours, depending on how many tests are taken
explanation: The manual states testing time can take from 1-2 hours depending on how many tests you take.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Missouri's Written Commercial Driver License Tests

question: A CDL holder who drives a CMV exclusively within one state, without crossing state lines or otherwise meeting interstate commerce criteria, is operating in what type of commerce?
explanation: Intrastate commerce is driving a CMV within a state without meeting any of the interstate commerce descriptions.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Medical Documentation Requirements

question: Which of the following is listed as an activity that qualifies a driver for 'excepted interstate commerce' status, exempting them from needing a medical examiner's certificate?
choice_a: Hauling hazardous materials across state lines
choice_c: Driving a for-hire passenger bus service
choice_d: Transporting school children and/or school staff between home and school
explanation: Transporting school children and/or school staff between home and school is listed as an excepted interstate commerce activity.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Inter/Intrastate Commerce

question: A driver who is required to have a 'certified' medical status but fails to keep an up-to-date medical examiner's certificate becomes what, potentially losing their CDL?
explanation: If a driver required to have a certified medical status fails to provide and keep up-to-date their medical examiner's certificate, they become 'not-certified' and may lose their CDL.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Medical Documentation Requirements

question: As of the compliance date of June 23, 2025, how must Medical Examiner's Certificate (MEC) information be submitted to the licensing agency?
choice_b: In person at any DMV office
choice_c: Electronically; paper certificate submissions are no longer accepted
explanation: As of the full compliance date of June 23, 2025, paper certificate submissions are no longer accepted, and MEC results are transmitted electronically from FMCSA's National Registry.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Medical Documentation

question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) makes it illegal to operate a CMV?
explanation: It is illegal to operate a CMV if your BAC is 0.04% or more.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Disqualifications

question: A first offense of driving a CMV with a BAC of 0.04% or more results in loss of CDL for at least how long?
explanation: A first offense for driving a CMV with a BAC of 0.04% or higher results in loss of the CDL for at least one year.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Disqualifications

question: If a first-offense CDL disqualification (such as a BAC violation) occurs while operating a vehicle placarded for hazardous materials, the disqualification period increases to at least how long?
explanation: The CDL disqualification period is at least three years if the offense occurs while operating a CMV placarded for hazardous materials.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Disqualifications

question: A second offense of an alcohol, controlled-substance, or CMV-related felony violation typically results in what disqualification?
explanation: You will lose your CDL for life for a second offense of the alcohol/felony/CMV violations described in the manual.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Disqualifications

question: 'Serious traffic violations' as defined in the manual include excessive speeding, defined as how many mph or more above the posted speed limit?
explanation: Excessive speeding as a serious traffic violation is defined as 15 mph or more above the posted speed limit.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Serious Traffic Violations

question: Two serious traffic violations within a three-year period involving a CMV result in a disqualification of at least how long?
explanation: Two serious traffic violations within a three-year period involving a CMV result in a disqualification of at least 60 days.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, 60-Day Disqualification

question: A CDL holder's first railroad-highway grade crossing violation results in a disqualification of at least how long?
explanation: A first railroad-highway grade crossing violation results in a disqualification of at least 60 days.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Railroad-highway Grade Crossing Violations

question: Which of the following is grounds for denial or loss of a hazardous materials endorsement after the required background check?
choice_a: Being wanted or under indictment for certain felonies
choice_b: Having a speeding ticket from five years ago
choice_d: Being a lawful permanent resident of the United States
explanation: Being wanted or under indictment for certain felonies is listed as grounds for denial or loss of a hazardous materials endorsement.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Hazardous Materials Endorsement Background Check

question: Missouri's manual distinguishes a 'Permanent Disqualification' from a 'Lifetime Disqualification.' Which offense results in a Permanent Disqualification?
choice_a: A first conviction for using a vehicle in the manufacture or illegal distribution of drugs, or a CMV in a severe human trafficking felony
choice_d: A second conviction for excessive speeding
explanation: Permanent Disqualification applies to a first conviction for using a motor vehicle in the manufacture or illegal distribution of drugs, or a first conviction of using a CMV in the commission of a severe human trafficking felony.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Permanent Disqualification

question: An 'Imminent Hazard Disqualification' may be imposed by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration for up to how long?
explanation: An Imminent Hazard Disqualification, based on an FMCSA determination that a person's driving constitutes an imminent hazard, may not exceed one year.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Imminent Hazard Disqualification

question: What is the rule regarding holding more than one driver's license while operating a CMV?
choice_a: It is allowed if one license is a CLP
choice_b: It is allowed as long as both are from the same state
choice_c: A driver cannot have more than one license; violators may be fined up to $5,000 or jailed, and other licenses are returned/canceled
choice_d: There is no rule against holding multiple licenses
explanation: You cannot have more than one license; breaking this rule can result in a fine up to $5,000 or jail, keeping only your home state license.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Other CDL Rules

question: Within how many days must a CDL holder notify their employer of a conviction for any traffic violation (except parking), regardless of which vehicle they were driving?
explanation: A driver must notify their employer within 30 days of conviction for any traffic violation (except parking), no matter what type of vehicle was involved.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Other CDL Rules

question: Within how many business days must a driver notify their employer if their license is suspended, revoked, or canceled, or they are disqualified from driving?
explanation: A driver must notify their employer within two business days of a suspension, revocation, cancellation, or disqualification.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Other CDL Rules

question: How many years of previous driving-job history must a CDL applicant provide to an employer when applying for a commercial driving job?
explanation: A CDL applicant must give their employer information on all driving jobs held for the past 10 years.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Other CDL Rules

question: A driver with a hazardous materials endorsement must notify and surrender the endorsement to the issuing state within how many hours of a disqualifying conviction, indictment, or related finding?
explanation: A driver with a hazardous materials endorsement must notify and surrender the endorsement within 24 hours of a disqualifying conviction or related finding.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Other CDL Rules

question: According to the manual, drivers are prohibited from doing which of the following while operating a CMV?
choice_a: Sending or reading text messages, and dialing a mobile phone by pressing more than a single button
explanation: Drivers are not allowed to hold a mobile phone to conduct a call or dial by pressing more than one button, and are not allowed to send or read text messages while driving.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Other CDL Rules

question: What safety equipment does the manual require a CMV driver to use at all times while operating a commercial motor vehicle?
explanation: Drivers must be properly restrained by a safety belt at all times while operating a CMV; unbelted drivers are four times more likely to be fatally injured if thrown from the vehicle.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, Other CDL Rules

question: Under Missouri's Employer Responsibilities, an employer may not knowingly allow a driver to operate a CMV during suspension, revocation, cancellation, disqualification, an out-of-service order, or when the driver holds more than one license. How is this violation classified?
choice_a: A felony only if injury results
choice_b: A minor infraction with no penalty
choice_d: A civil fine only, capped at $100
explanation: The manual states this violation is a Class A misdemeanor.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Employer Responsibilities

question: Under Missouri's Employee Responsibilities, a CDL holder convicted of a violation (other than parking) in another state must notify the Director of Revenue within how many days?
explanation: A CDL holder must notify the Director of Revenue of any out-of-state violation other than parking within 30 days of conviction.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Employee Responsibilities

question: Per Missouri's Employee Responsibilities section, when must a driver notify their employer of a license suspension, revocation, cancellation, or disqualification?
choice_a: By the end of the business day after receiving notice
explanation: Missouri's Employee Responsibilities require notifying the employer of a suspension, revocation, cancellation, disqualification, or out-of-service order by the end of the business day after the driver receives notice.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Employee Responsibilities

question: The International Registration Plan (IRP) provides for the equitable collection and distribution of what, for vehicles operating across the 48 contiguous states and Canadian provinces?
explanation: The IRP and IFTA are federally mandated programs providing for the equitable collection and distribution of vehicle license fees and motor fuels taxes.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, International Registration Plan

question: Under IRP/IFTA record-keeping requirements, original Individual Vehicle Distance Records (IVDRs) must be maintained for a minimum of how many years?
explanation: IVDR records must be maintained for a minimum of four years, as they serve as the source document for fee and tax calculations.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, International Registration Plan

question: What is the minimum age to apply for an intrastate-only Missouri CDL?
explanation: Missouri CDL eligibility age is 18 years for intrastate driving (until age 21).
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Missouri CDL Eligibility

question: What is the minimum age to hold a Missouri CDL for interstate driving (if otherwise eligible)?
explanation: Missouri CDL eligibility age for interstate driving is 21 years, if otherwise eligible.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Missouri CDL Eligibility

question: To apply for a new, renewal, or duplicate Missouri CDL, how many forms of residence address verification must an applicant submit?
explanation: Applicants must submit two forms of residence address verification to apply for a new, renewal, or duplicate CDL.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Missouri CDL Eligibility

question: A driver holding a commercial driver's license issued under the Canadian National Safety Code or a Licencia Federal de Conductor from Mexico is prohibited from obtaining what, unless they obtain U.S. permanent resident status or citizenship?
choice_a: A Missouri CLP written test appointment
choice_d: A non-domiciled CDL, or any other type of driver's license, from a U.S. jurisdiction
explanation: Under the single license provision of 49 CFR 383.21, such a driver is prohibited from obtaining a non-domiciled CDL or any other type of driver's license from a U.S. jurisdiction until obtaining permanent resident status or citizenship.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Missouri Non-Domiciled Commercial Driver License

question: A non-domiciled CDL applicant in Missouri must be employed by a Missouri-based employer and provide an employment letter dated within how many days of the application?
explanation: Nondomiciled CDL applicants must provide an employment letter dated within 30 days of the application.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Missouri Employment: Nondomiciled CDL Applicants

question: What is the fee for a Missouri CDL issued for a term of 3 years or less?
explanation: The fee for a Missouri CDL issued for a term of 3 years or less is $20.00.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, CDL License Fees and Expiration

question: What is the fee for a Missouri Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP), issued for a term of 1 year (360 days) or less?
explanation: The fee for a Missouri CLP issued for 1 year (360 days) or less is $10.00.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, CDL License Fees and Expiration

question: What are the separate fees for the Missouri CDL Written Test and the CDL Skills Test?
explanation: The CDL Written Test Fee and the CDL Skills Test Fee are each $25.00.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, CDL License Fees and Expiration

question: A CDL with a School Bus endorsement issued to a driver aged 75 or over has a maximum term of how many years, and what is its fee?
explanation: A CDL with a School Bus Endorsement for a driver aged 75 or over has a 2-year term and a fee of $7.50.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, CDL License Fees and Expiration

question: What is the minimum age to apply for a Missouri Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
explanation: You must be at least 18 years old to apply for a Missouri Commercial Learner's Permit.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)

question: Which of the following endorsements can NEVER be added to a Missouri CLP?
explanation: A CLP cannot be issued with a motorcycle, double/triple trailer, or hazardous materials endorsement; only P, S, and N may be added.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)

question: A CLP holder operating a CMV must be accompanied by whom?
choice_a: No one; CLP holders may drive alone
choice_b: A CDL holder valid for the vehicle being operated, seated beside or reasonably near the CLP holder
choice_c: A state-certified driving instructor, regardless of license type
choice_d: Any licensed driver with a regular driver's license
explanation: A CLP allows the holder to operate a CMV when accompanied by a CDL holder valid for that vehicle, seated beside them (or reasonably near, in the case of buses).
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)

question: A Missouri CLP is issued for a term of one year (360 days) or less. Can it be renewed?
choice_a: Only with special written permission from the Highway Patrol
choice_c: No, it cannot be renewed; retesting is required if additional training is needed beyond expiration
explanation: A Missouri CLP is issued for one year (360 days) or a lesser term and cannot be renewed; if additional training is needed beyond expiration, retesting is required.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)

question: A CLP holder must hold the CLP for training purposes for a minimum of how many calendar days before taking the CDL skills test?
explanation: Drivers must hold the CLP for training purposes a minimum of 14 calendar days before skills testing.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Skills Testing

question: If a CLP holder does not complete all skills testing requirements during the initial CLP term, what must they do?
choice_a: Immediately receive a full CDL by default
choice_c: Pay a late fee and continue with the same CLP
choice_d: Retake the required written examinations to obtain a new CLP, and previously passed skills segments become invalid
explanation: If skills testing is not completed during the initial CLP term, previously passed segments must be retaken, and the applicant must retake the required written examinations to obtain a new CLP.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Skills Testing

question: Missouri requires completion of an FMCSA-approved Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) program before testing for which of the following?
choice_b: A CDL renewal with no change in class or endorsement
choice_c: A first-time CDL, a first-time hazmat/passenger/school bus endorsement, or an upgrade in CDL classification
choice_d: A driver's license reinstatement after a parking ticket
explanation: An FMCSA-approved ELDT program is required before hazardous materials knowledge or skills testing when applying for a first-time CDL, a first-time hazmat/passenger/school bus endorsement, or an upgrade in classification.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Mandatory Entry Level Driver Training

question: What happens if a Missouri CDL examiner cannot electronically confirm an applicant's completion of mandatory ELDT?
choice_a: The examiner will administer the test anyway
choice_b: The applicant is automatically enrolled in ELDT on the spot
choice_c: The applicant receives a temporary waiver
choice_d: The examiner will deny administration of the hazardous materials endorsement knowledge test or CDL skills test
explanation: Missouri CDL examiners will deny administration of a hazardous materials endorsement knowledge test or CDL skills test if completion of mandatory ELDT cannot be confirmed electronically.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Mandatory Entry Level Driver Training

question: Under RSMo 302.720, the Director of Revenue may waive the CDL written and/or driving skills test for which group?
choice_a: Qualified current or former members of the U.S. armed forces, subject to certain conditions
choice_b: Any driver with a clean 10-year record
explanation: Under RSMo 302.720, the Director of Revenue may waive the CDL written and driving skills test, or the driving skills test only, for qualified current or former members of the U.S. armed forces.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Military Exemption

question: An applicant who is eligible only for a waiver of the driving skills test under the military exemption must still do what?
choice_b: Wait an additional 90 days before applying
choice_d: Pay double the standard licensing fee
explanation: Applicants eligible only for waiver of the driving skills test must complete all applicable written tests.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Military Exemption

question: Which of the following drivers is exempt from the CDL law under Missouri's manual?
choice_a: A common carrier transporting general freight
choice_b: A rideshare driver operating a passenger van
choice_c: A farmer (or family member/employee) transporting agricultural products or farm machinery within 150 miles of the farm
choice_d: A contractor transporting hazardous placarded materials
explanation: A person transporting agricultural products, farm machinery, or farm supplies within 150 miles of the farm, if the driver is a farmer, family member, or employee, is exempt from the CDL law.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Exemptions

question: Military personnel are exempt from CDL requirements when driving CMVs for military purposes. Which group is included in this exemption?
choice_a: Retired military personnel driving personal vehicles
choice_c: Active duty military personnel, reservists/national guard on full-time training duty, and national guard military technicians
explanation: The CDL law exemption for military personnel includes active duty military, reservists/national guard on 'Full-time Training Duty' or 'Inactive Duty for Training,' and national guard military technicians.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Exemptions

question: Which type of equipment is listed as exempt from CDL requirements as 'certain construction equipment not intended for use on the highway'?
choice_d: Backhoes, motor graders, motor scrapers, excavators, and bulldozers
explanation: Certain construction equipment not intended for highway use, such as backhoes, motor graders, motor scrapers, excavators, and bulldozers, is exempt from the CDL law.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, Exemptions

question: Under Missouri's point system, how many points accumulated within 18 months results in a license suspension?
explanation: Under Missouri's point system, 8 points accumulated in 18 months results in a suspension.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, The Point System

question: Which of the following point totals results in a license REVOCATION under Missouri's point system?
explanation: Missouri's point system revokes a license at 12 points in 12 months (or 18 points in 24 months, or 24 points in 36 months), while 8 points in 18 months results in only a suspension.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, The Point System

question: For a first-offense BAC or DWI violation, what must a driver do to have driving privileges reinstated, according to the manual?
choice_c: Wait 5 years with no other requirements
choice_d: Pay a $45 reinstatement fee, attend SATOP, and provide proof of insurance
explanation: For a first offense of refusal to submit to a BAC test, BAC 0.08% or more, or DWI, the driver must pay a $45 reinstatement fee, attend a Substance Awareness Traffic Offender Program (SATOP), and provide proof of insurance.
source_note: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 14, First Offense - How to Get Your License Back
